srs.title: UPI-based Digital Payments Application (RE Compliance Module) - SRS Overview
srs.summary: The system is a mobile application enabling customers of Regulated Entities (REs) to initiate UPI payments (Send/Receive), perform Scan-and-Pay at merchants via a third-party Payment Gateway, and monitor transactions. The system must enforce a flat ₹50,000 transaction cap across all UPI actions and,
assumptions: The 'third-party Payment Gateway' integration will provide native, PCI-P2PE compliant tokenization for card details on merchant POS terminals.
The third-party Payment Gateway handles the direct connectivity to NPCI/UPI Hub for card transactions, as the user declined direct external merchant integration.
The flat ₹50,000 cap applies strictly to individual transaction amounts, not cumulative daily limits.

The user's definition of 'high-velocity' (3 attempts in 5 minutes) is the sole acceptable trigger for fraud alerts; scenarios involving successful transactions but suspicious post-authentication behavior are out of scope.

risks.title: Compliance Risk (PCI-DSS & PCI-P2PE)
risks.text: Failure to ensure the third-party gateway solution is certified under PCI-P2PE (evidence E1) or PCI-DSS (evidence E3) creates a legal and reputational liability for the bank if card data is not end-to

risks.title: Regulatory Risk (Transaction Limits & Monitoring)
risks.text: The proposed flat ₹50,000 cap and fixed velocity rules may not align with the RE's risk appetite or specific regulatory mandates (evidence E4) requiring limits to be 'commensurate with their risk' and

risks.title: Functional Gap: New Beneficiary Validation
risks.text: The user's answers define failure limits for login authentication (evidence E2) but do not specify rules for 'transaction velocity' in the context of adding new beneficiaries, a high-risk activity

openIssues: The brief's requirement for 'Scan-and-Pay' conflicts with the user's decision to integrate with a 'third-party Payment Gateway for merchant card'. Clarify if the app supports scanning UPI QR codes at merchants or only initiating card transactions remotely.

The user defined failed auth attempts as the trigger for alerts. Evidence E2 suggests alerts are also required for 'failed log-in', but also implies a need to monitor 'transaction velocity' for specific high-risk scenarios (e.g., overseas cash withdrawals).
The scope for 'Transaction Limits' is ambiguous between static product caps and dynamic risk-based limits mandated by the Card Network (BIN/Card) (evidence E4).

requirements.statement: The system shall enforce a flat monetary cap of ₹50,000 across all UPI actions (UPI Pay, UPI Request, Mini Statement) by default.
requirements.acceptance: The system automatically blocks or flags any UPI transaction where the total amount exceeds ₹50,000, regardless of the specific UPI product type used.

requirements.statement: The system shall trigger fraud alerts only for high-velocity failed authentication attempts, defined strictly as more than 3 failed attempts within a 5-minute window.
requirements.acceptance: The system generates a verified alert if >3 failed authentication attempts occur within any 5-minute period and does not alert on isolated failed attempts under this threshold.

requirements.statement: The system shall integrate with a third-party Payment Gateway for processing external merchant card transactions, adhering to PCI-P2PE standards for data encryption.
requirements.acceptance: The integration is verified to encrypt card information instantly upon initial capture (swipe) and transmit it directly to the payment processor without storing plain-text data at,

requirements.statement: The system shall block user access to the digital payment product immediately after a maximum of 5 failed login or authentication attempts.
requirements.acceptance: Testing confirms that the 6th failed login attempt triggers an immediate account lockout, and a secure re-activation procedure is provided via email or SMS notification.

requirements.statement: The system shall log all Hardware Security Module (HSM) access events, ensuring logs are tamper-proof, and maintain clustered HSMs for high availability with secure backups.
requirements.acceptance: System logs generated by the HSM pass tamper-evidence checks, and the architecture diagram confirms HSM nodes are clustered with automated secure backup replication enabled.

requirements.statement: The system shall encrypt all sensitive customer data (account details, payment credentials, transaction data) at rest in the database and never store card details in plain text.
requirements.acceptance: Audit logs confirm 100% of stored customer payment credentials are encrypted; no queries return unencrypted plain-text card data from the RE database.

requirements.statement: The system shall implement rules to detect suspicious transactional behaviors, including high-velocity transactions, high-risk Merchant Category Codes (MCC), and transaction patterns for new app users
requirements.acceptance: The system successfully flags test scenarios containing defined velocity (e.g., >3 transactions in 5 mins) or new-user patterns as 'suspicious' and triggers the configured alerting

sdlc.justification: The 'Agile–V-Model hybrid' (94/100) is the optimal selection because this project presents a paradox: it requires the rigorous verification and formal security validation of a V-Model (due to High Regulatory Criticality per R1-R8 and High Security Risk per R2, R4-R7) while simultaneously needing the adaptability of Agile to accommodate High Expected Change Frequency per R8 and dynamic rule engines per R1/R7. A pure V-Model would be too slow for evolving transaction limits and rules, whereas a pure Agile model would lack the necessary formality for PCI-P2PE compliance and fraud rule validation.

workflow.activities: Executive workshops to align on RBI mandates (R8), PCI-P2PE (R3), and RE guidelines.
workflow.roles: Product Owner (Regulatory Lead), Chief Security Officer, Compliance VP
workflow.deliverables: Project Charter, Initial Risk Register, High-Level Architecture Design (HLAD), Compliant Data Model
workflow.gate: User Acceptance: Business approval of compliance alignment and budget

workflow.activities: Detailed functional/spec analysis for the immutable core; User story definition for variable rules.
workflow.roles: System Analysts (Secure Coding Specialist), Business Analysts, Lead QA
workflow.deliverables: Functional Spec Document (FSD), Security Threat Model (initial), Use Case Diagrams
workflow.gate: Security: Initial Threat Model review and sign-off

workflow.activities: Detailed system design with 'Secure by Design' principles; API contract definition.
workflow.roles: System Architects, Lead Security Engineers, DevOps Engineers
workflow.deliverables: System Design Document (SDD), Security Architecture (Cryptography/TLS), Data Flow Diagrams (DFD)
workflow.gate: Security: Architecture Review Board (ARB) approval; Compliance: PCI-DSS scope confirmation

workflow.activities: Sprint-based development of the digital payment product; parallel unit testing.
workflow.roles: Full Stack Developers, Security Engineers, QA Engineers
workflow.deliverables: Testable Software Builds, Unit Test Cases, Code Coverage Reports
workflow.gate: Compliance: Static Application Security Testing (SAST) and Dependency Scan pass

workflow.activities: System Testing (ST), Security Validation (VA), Penetration Testing (PT), Compliance Validation.
workflow.roles: QA Engineers, Security Auditors, External Third-Party Pen Testers, Reg
workflow.deliverables: Test Summaries, ST Report, PT Report, Compliance Validation Report (CVE/PCI)
workflow.gate: Compliance/Human: Mandatory Regulatory sign-off for Fraud Rules (R2, R7, R8) and Cap (R1); PT execution

workflow.activities: Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) to Production; Monitoring setup.
workflow.roles: DevOps Engineers, Release Managers, Security Ops
workflow.deliverables: Production Release, Runbooks, Security Incident Response Plan
workflow.gate: Human: Change Advisory Board (CAB) approval for production release

ranking.why: high regulation with evolving requirements: iterations plus V-Model verification gates
risk-driven loops for high uncertainty or technical risk
strict verification and validation: every build phase has a matching test phase
continuous secure deployment with automated security checks
short iterations absorb frequently changing requirements
rapid prototyping for small, low-risk systems

rejected.why: heavy risk analysis each loop is costly when requirements are clear
rigid once a phase closes; late changes are expensive
its value is continuous delivery, which this project needs little of
light documentation clashes with formal audit and sign-off
too little rigour for high-risk or regulated systems
testing comes late, so verification evidence arrives after design is locked

item.text: Done. **Agile–V-Model hybrid** fits best: 6 phases, each with an exit gate tied to requirement IDs.
